source.title: On the Recall Scaling Laws in Mamba: A Theoretical and Mechanistic Study via Hashing
source.authors: Yuval Koren; Assaf Ben-Kish; Raja Giryes; Lior Wolf; Itamar Zimerman

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and mathematical notation are flattened or imperfectly rendered.
record.tranche_reason: The study develops and tests scaling laws for associative-recall accuracy in Mamba on synthetic AR/MQAR tasks. It does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss, downstream-task performance, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, and it does not rely on the claim as a tool.
record.gate_note: The paper reports recall-accuracy results as embedding dimension, state size, depth, and head pattern vary. These are about a distinct metric and task from the claim’s held-out pretraining loss; the paper’s statement that associative recall correlates with language-modeling performance does not make its recall results tests of the claim versions. It also mentions prior perplexity ablations from another paper, which are cited results and not rows here.
record.test_reason: The study derives and tests 'recall scaling laws' for Mamba on synthetic AR/MQAR tasks, where recall accuracy follows a normal-CDF form in N·D/Nf and log V. It never measures held-out pretraining loss, compute-optimal allocation, or downstream-task performance, and it does not use the Kaplan/Hoffmann laws as a tool. The shared name 'scaling laws' is the only link. Its mention of Mamba-2 perplexity ablations cites another paper's results.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude that Mamba performs recall through a learned hash-like (JL-projection) compression circuit. Their theory predicts the dimensions needed and the recall probability, and it matches trained simplified and full models. Model dimensions D and N are the main capacity bottleneck.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and analyzes Mamba on synthetic associative-recall tasks and measures recall accuracy across model dimensions and architectures. The original claim concerns held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy, scaling with parameters, tokens, and compute, and compute-optimal data/model allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported recall outcomes vary with task (AR versus MQAR), model type (linear versus full), layer count, Mamba-2 head pattern, and whether keys repeat. The full-model scaling coefficient is described as heuristically determined. Accuracy grids use best-of-seeds results to represent capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic AR/MQAR recall accuracy in simplified and full Mamba collapses onto a curve of the form Φ(sqrt(ND/(aNf+N)) − sqrt(2 log V)). Multi-layer models depend on ΛN, and only the MHA head pattern improves recall at fixed D.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mamba associative-recall capacity scales with state × embedding dimension relative to facts × log vocabulary, following a normal-CDF law rather than a power law in loss.

fits_no_version.finding: In circuit ablations, removing the gate, activation or discretisation keeps MQAR accuracy at 1.00. Removing the convolution drops it to 0.06, roughly the 1/Nf guessing rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The convolution's copy-and-shift step is necessary for key-value binding in Mamba's recall circuit.

fits_no_version.finding: With repeated keys, single-layer accuracy is about 1/Nk, and the paper reports that depth resolves this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overwriting stale key-value entries requires depth of two or more layers in simplified Mamba.

record.problems: The empirical results concern synthetic associative-recall accuracy rather than held-out language-model loss. Many scaling-curve values are shown in figures rather than tabulated; the paper reports best-of-seeds accuracy to represent capacity, not optimization success probability. The full-model scaling coefficient is determined heuristically, and the authors note that the analysis relies on simplified models and does not fully characterize each component of full Mamba.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were omitted from the reported findings recorded here. The paper’s cited language-model perplexity ablations from Mamba-2 (Section 5.4) are prior-work results, not this study’s own measurements, so they are not included.

untested.parts: No pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, tokens or compute.
No extrapolation of loss fits from small runs to larger ones.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters and tokens.
Depth, state size and head-pattern variations are measured on synthetic recall accuracy, not on loss at fixed parameter count.
No loss-scaling test in other modalities or regimes. The synthetic recall-accuracy law has a normal-CDF form, not a power law in loss.
No downstream-task benchmark. Associative recall is the training task itself, and its link to language-model performance is only cited.
No comparison of fitting choices for loss exponents or for compute-optimal splits.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly unlinked to any version (all ['none']) and their state cannot_determine is appropriate. 'Recall scaling laws' share a name with the claim but concern a different construct. No row needs fixing.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No test of whether loss fits on smaller language-model runs predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation experiment measuring loss-minimising parameter and token counts.
The paper varies depth and Mamba-2 head patterns for recall accuracy, not loss at fixed parameter count; it does not test width or general architecture effects on pretraining loss.
No tests of the claimed loss scaling in other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The reported outcome is synthetic associative-recall accuracy, not downstream-task performance or its relationship to pretraining loss.
No test of how published pretraining-loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations change with fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: Trained linear Mamba
rows.size_stated: D and N varied; specific values not stated for the scaling-curve result.
rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding dimension D and state size N and measured recall accuracy.
rows.measure: Recall accuracy; reported scaling form uses x = 1/σ and a = 1, with b approximately √(2 log V).
rows.value: Accuracy follows approximately p_recall(x) ≈ Φ(x − b), with a = 1 and b ≈ √(2 log V).
rows.note: This is a recall-accuracy scaling result, not a held-out cross-entropy result.

rows.subject: Trained linear Mamba
rows.size_stated: D and N varied; specific values not stated for the scaling-curve result.
rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding dimension D and state size N and measured recall accuracy.
rows.measure: Recall accuracy; the unified scaling form reports a ≈ 5/4 for MQAR and b ≈ √(2 log V).
rows.value: Accuracy follows approximately p_recall(x) ≈ Φ(x − b), with a ≈ 5/4 and b ≈ √(2 log V).
rows.note: The main text’s flattened notation renders the coefficient as “54”; Appendix F.5 gives the coefficient as 5/4. This is recall accuracy, not pretraining loss.

rows.subject: Trained full nonlinear Mamba
rows.size_stated: D and N varied; specific values not stated for the scaling-curve result.
rows.operation_detail: Varied embedding dimension D and state size N and measured recall accuracy.
rows.measure: Recall accuracy; the fitted coefficient is reported relative to the linear model’s coefficient.
rows.value: The full model also fits the recall scaling form, with a_full ≈ 1/2 a_linear, determined heuristically.
rows.note: The authors describe the full model as having improved recall performance under a similar scaling behavior. This is not a comparison of pretraining loss.

rows.subject: Trained linear Mamba
rows.operation_detail: Measured recall accuracy while varying vocabulary size and context length.
rows.measure: Recall-accuracy scaling against vocabulary size; per-context-length linear-fit slopes are reported.
rows.value: Per-L fit slopes are 1.18–1.56; the authors say this is consistent with the theoretical slope of 1 as the theoretical scaling is approximate.
rows.note: This measures recall accuracy, not language-model loss.

rows.subject: Simplified multi-layer Mamba
rows.size_stated: D, N, and layer count Λ varied; specific grid dimensions not stated in the result text.
rows.operation_detail: Varied state size N and layer count Λ and measured recall accuracy.
rows.measure: Recall accuracy as a function of effective state size and the scaling variable.
rows.value: The paper reports that accuracy is determined by Neff = ΛN and collapses onto a curve approximately following p_recall(x) ≈ Φ(x − b), with b ≈ √(2 log V).
rows.locator: Sections 5.3 and Appendix A.1, Figures 5 and 10
rows.note: The outcome is recall accuracy rather than pretraining loss.

rows.subject: Simplified multi-layer Mamba
rows.size_stated: Examples with (N, Λ) = (12, 1), (6, 2), (4, 3), and (3, 4); D not stated for this example.
rows.operation_detail: Compared recall for different N and Λ combinations with the same effective state size.
rows.value: pMQAR ≈ 0.38 at each listed configuration, as reported in the text.
rows.note: This is an architecture/recall result, not a loss-scaling result.

rows.subject: Simplified Mamba-2 with MVA pattern
rows.size_stated: D, N, and head count M varied; specific values not stated for the summary comparison.
rows.operation_detail: Compared recall across Mamba-2 multi-head patterns with D held fixed in the experiment.
rows.value: Theoretical result states pMVA = psingle; experiments describe MVA as matching the single-head baseline.

rows.subject: Simplified Mamba-2 with MQA pattern
rows.size_stated: D held fixed; N and M varied; specific values not stated for the summary result.
rows.operation_detail: Compared recall across Mamba-2 multi-head patterns.
rows.value: The theoretical result gives pMQA ≤ psingle; experiments report MQA as weaker than MVA.

rows.subject: Simplified Mamba-2 with MKA pattern
rows.size_stated: D held fixed; N and M varied; specific values not stated for the summary result.
rows.operation_detail: Compared recall across Mamba-2 multi-head patterns.
rows.value: The theoretical result gives pMKA ≤ psingle; experiments report MKA as weaker than MVA.

rows.subject: Simplified Mamba-2 with MHA pattern
rows.size_stated: D held fixed; N and M varied; specific values not stated for the summary result.
rows.operation_detail: Compared recall across Mamba-2 multi-head patterns.
rows.value: The theoretical result bounds pMHA between psingle[D,N] and psingle[D,MN]; the experiments report improvement only for MHA, which enlarges both key and query dimensions.

rows.stage_stated: trained on MQAR with repeated keys

rows.baseline: Guessing among the Nk stored values, with accuracy 1/Nk
